A1.justification: Both complete, readable 17-page PDFs describe the same VPFA research. Text, equations, figures, tables and appendices can be matched despite the changed title, layout and added analyses.

before.justification: V1 reports original retrieval experiments, feature-correlation analyses, ablations, efficiency measurements and appendix experiments on robustness, cross-modal retrieval and cross-dataset transfer.

after.justification: V2 retains these empirical results and adds separate-resolution evaluations, backbone comparisons, feature-adaptation baselines and Grad-CAM examples.

M1.justification: V1 explicitly trains on identity-averaged LR–HR prototypes in Equation (2), Algorithm 1 and Section 5.2. V2 instead specifies individual image-pair features without identity averaging throughout Algorithm 1 and Sections 4.4 and 5.3. This substantially changes the reported training inputs and supervision, although the backbone, residual MLP and loss remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether retained experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: All result-bearing datasets and tasks are retained, including the appendix's MSMT17, MLRpro, RegDB and RSTPReid evaluations. Separate-resolution tests use already-covered downsampling levels. However, v2 removes DukeMTMC from one dataset list while retaining the MLR-DukeMTMC reference; neither version provides Duke-specific results. Whether this represents removed coverage or correction of an inconsistent description is unresolved.

E2.justification: V2 adds FiLM, Adapter and mean-vector offset comparisons in Table 9, plus original TransReID-DeiT and CLIP-ReID baselines in Table 8. These substantially broaden comparisons beyond v1's existing residual ablation and benchmark methods. Table 3 retains its comparator membership; changed Part Aligned and PyrNet citations are not method replacements.

E3.justification: V2 adds fixed 2×, 3× and 4× evaluations alongside mixed-resolution tests, additional backbone/framework configurations, and replacement-head comparisons with a shared training protocol and loss. Training-data preparation also changes from identity prototypes and identity-level shuffling to individual feature pairs and random shuffling. The stated 5,000-pair budget, optimizer, batch size and 120 epochs remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses examine sensitivity to resolution severity, generalization across feature extractors, and whether simpler adaptation heads suffice (Appendix A.2, A.4–A.5). Section 5.8 adds similarity-based Grad-CAM cases investigating matching cues. Existing residual, width, depth, feature-distance, retrieval and cross-domain analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same ten random splits and averages for CUHK03, VIPeR and CAVIAR, and the same Pearson-correlation standard deviations. V2 adds no new seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: All eleven original tables retain their numerical results, but v2 adds substantial results in Tables 7–9. Examples include 4× Rank-1 of 93.6 versus 85.6 without VPFA, CLIP-ReID CNN Rank-1 of 90.6 versus 88.2, and FiLM/Adapter Rank-1 of 92.1/91.8 versus VPFA's 94.1. These are new comparisons, not version-to-version gains. Table 7 also shows a 2× Rank-5 decline from 98.2 to 97.8. Section 5.5 newly reports TransReID throughput of 80.80 samples/second.

T1.justification: V1's Equation (2), defining identity-averaged training prototypes, is removed from v2's formulation. The residual mapping, squared-error loss and law-of-cosines derivation remain equivalent. The new low-rank interpretation is not developed into a formal theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain discovery of a resolution-related feature direction, lightweight frozen-backbone VPFA, strong benchmark performance and broader applicability. V2's abstract explicitly mentions averaging, but this qualification already appears in v1's introduction. The contribution list and conclusion retain their substantive claims.

C2.justification: New Section 7 states that the analyses do not prove a universal one-dimensional direction, suggests a possibly low-rank, input-dependent subspace, and identifies limitations from missing identity information and untested real-world degradations. It positions VPFA as complementary to reconstruction methods. V2 also adds Grad-CAM mechanism interpretations and explicitly limits backbone comparisons to matched within-framework settings.

D1.justification: V2 revises feature-pair construction instructions, documents the Grad-CAM score and gradient target, and adds backbone and comparison-control information. Most implementation details remain unchanged, including dimensions, initialization, optimizer settings and code link. Hardware information moves from Appendix A.1 to Section 5.2 rather than being newly disclosed; alternative-head configurations remain described only as standard.

R1.justification: V2 adds FiLM and Houlsby-style Adapter references and a focused discussion positioning VPFA against general feature adaptation. It adds Zhao et al. for Part Aligned, reattributes PyrNet to Martinel et al., and removes the Gong and Goodfellow references. The main ReID and cross-resolution related-work narrative remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 retitles the paper, rewrites the abstract and training passages, and expands comparator explanations while retaining most existing prose and the main scientific section sequence. It moves environment details into the main text, adds limitations, impact and acknowledgements sections, and removes the LLM-use disclosure.

P2.justification: The single-column preprint becomes a two-column conference-style main text. Figure 2 is substantially redesigned with training and inference diagrams; Grad-CAM Figure 4 and Tables 7–9 are added. Existing tables and t-SNE panels are rearranged, while the original retrieval figure and appendix tables are retained under new numbering.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens methodological support: Tables 8–9 address v1's limited validation across backbones and against general feature-adaptation alternatives, while Section 7 meaningfully qualifies the interpretation of the correlation evidence. These gains improve the justification and scientific caution without relying on higher headline scores. Reproducibility remains imperfect: some added settings are underspecified, and the revised pairwise-training description is not reconciled with the unchanged legacy results.
